SMTO-MAN-0002 — This Manual page isn't available

GUID: 1b1de5ca-6b11-4ec5-8a69-96e530e92f9a
Slug: manual-document-not-found
Domain: MAN · Subsystem: man

What happened

  • The Manual link you opened points to a page this version of the Manual doesn't have. It may be an old bookmark, a mistyped link, or a page that was renamed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Manual from the navigation menu and type the topic or error code into the Search manual box. Search only lists pages this version actually contains, so it finds the page under its current name.
  2. If you came from an error message, go back to it and select Explain this error again. The error panel builds a fresh link to that error's current Manual page.
  3. If pages for error codes are missing but other pages open, tell the person who manages SMTO. Error-code pages are built when the Manual starts, and if that step failed only those pages are missing.

What success looks like

  • The Manual shows the page's title and text instead of the error.

If it still fails

  • Copy the link you opened and the error details, and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Replace any old bookmark with the link you get from search.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Manual service returned 404 because the validated document ID has no entry in the current corpus snapshot (a stale or mistyped link, a removed or renamed document, or generated reference pages that were not published).

What this means

  • Manual document or related-document lookup returns no payload for the requested document in the current corpus. Manual lookup diagnostics describe local snapshot availability and validation. They neither fetch external documentation nor rebuild content during rendering; generated-lane failure does not invalidate an available authored corpus.

Why this can happen

  • Manual document or related-document lookup returns no payload for the requested document in the current corpus.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the current index and installed build before assuming a link's historical target still exists.

How to fix it

  • Check the ID against GET /api/manual/catalog and the document count in /healthz. If generated pages such as error-smto-* are missing, check the Manual service log for a failed generated-reference build at startup (docs_generated_cache_failures); authored pages are still served.
  • Open the current Manual index and search for the document or immutable Error ID.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A current index or error Explain link opens the intended available page.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Manual lookup diagnostics describe local snapshot availability and validation. They neither fetch external documentation nor rebuild content during rendering; generated-lane failure does not invalidate an available authored corpus.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
